findings.description: Vocabulary/mechanism mismatch between spec and code, visible from both sides. SHEET-TAB-003's whole claim is framed around named Google Sheets objects: 'only saved Sheets Filter Views survive a republish' (Filter Views are THE survivor) and 'a basic filter, a manual sort, or a human-inserted row ... is overwritten by design' (these are THE casualties, named explicitly). The real implementation (adapters.rs's ViewSheetsAdapter, lib.rs's SheetsViewClient trait, testkit.rs's InMemorySheetsView, tabs.rs) contains zero code, fields, comments, or tests mentioning Filter Views, basic filters, or sort at all — the actual 'regenerated' mechanism is a single generic structural rule instead: a frozen header (row 1) plus a fixed DATA_START_ROW=2 anchor, with a wholesale tail-truncated rewrite of everything from row 2 down. Direction A: forced by the literal spec text, all three A-runs independently invented explicit handling/reasoning for Filter Views and basic filters that has no counterpart in the real code — A1 built a full FilterViewSpec type plus get_filter_views/add_filter_view/rebind snapshot-restore API; A2 added an explicit clear_basic_filter trait method and the comment 'Deliberately NO delete_filter_view / no sort-order API exposed here'; A3 added a debug_assert guarding that the request builder never emits a DeleteFilterViewRequest. None of this exists in the real SheetsViewClient trait (batch_update_view / set_tab_order / read_price_pass / write_stale_banner only) or its ViewSheetsAdapter implementation. Direction B: none of B1/B2/B3, reconstructing purely from the code, ever surface a Filter-View or basic-filter concept — because the code gives them nothing to reconstruct; the real mechanism they all describe (frozen header, DATA_START_ROW, tail-truncate) never engages with the spec's named objects at all. Both directions are pointing at the same underlying incoherence: the spec narrates 'regenerated' at the level of Sheets UI features, the code implements it at the level of a row anchor + a header invariant, and neither side's text ever bridges the two.

The code pins a hard, load-bearing invariant that SHEET-TAB-003's text never states at all: the header (row 1) is frozen, written exactly once — only on first tab creation via the missing-tab bootstrap path in ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view (ensure_sheet + one update_range to 'TAB!A1' + the data write) — and every subsequent republish must present a byte-identical header, enforced unconditionally via `assert_eq!(existing.header, tab.header, "the frozen header must never be rewritten on republish")` in InMemorySheetsView::batch_update_view (a hard panic in any build, not release-stripped). All three B runs converge tightly on this exact mechanism and the exact constant DATA_START_ROW=2 (B1's SHEET-VIEW-PUB-01/02/10, B2's 'the header SHALL be written exactly once ... and SHALL NEVER be rewritten,' B3's UB1) plus the same missing-tab-creates-header-once path and the same tail-truncate-to-exact-row-count semantics (confirmed by tabs.rs's republish_regenerates_data_and_never_rewrites_frozen_header test: 2 rows then republished with 1 row, header unchanged, rows.len()==1). None of this — the anchor row, the once-only write timing, the hard-panic contract — traces to any text in SHEET-TAB-003, which talks only about Filter Views, basic filter, manual sort, and human-inserted rows. There is also a mild literal tension worth naming: EARS says 'ONLY saved Sheets Filter Views survive a republish,' but the code makes the header a second, deliberately-preserved, contract-enforced survivor — the spec's exclusivity claim ('only') is narrower than what the code actually guarantees.

The 'read-only' half of SHEET-TAB-003 leaves the enforcement mechanism completely open, and the three A-runs disagree with each other on it, which weakens (rather than strengthens) this as a clean finding. A1 and A2 both assume read-only is enforced purely by convention — no ACL/protected-range call, just 'no mutation API besides republish is exposed' — which actually matches the real code's posture (neither SheetsViewClient nor ViewSheetsAdapter exposes any protected-range or ACL call anywhere in adapters.rs or lib.rs). A3 instead invents an explicit soft lock (`set_protected_range(sheet_id, warning_only: true)` called on every republish) that has no counterpart in the real implementation at all. Because A1/A2 and A3 land on genuinely different answers to a spec-forced sub-decision, this is better read as A-side instability on an underspecified point than a confirmed drift — but it does confirm, by two of three runs guessing correctly, that 'read-only' in the real system is enforced by nothing more than the absence of an exposed write API, a fact SHEET-TAB-003's text never states explicitly.

notes: Read all four real files in full (lib.rs, adapters.rs, testkit.rs, tabs.rs) rather than relying on the pasted A/B excerpts alone. The B-direction reconstructions pull in a good deal of material (advisory write-lock behavior, per-tab stale banner/retry, set_tab_order reassert, settle-pass serialization) that is real and tightly agreed-upon across B1/B2/B3, but scoped strictly to SHEET-TAB-003's text (read-only/regenerated/Filter-View-survival/basic-filter-sort-row-overwrite) rather than the whole republish subsystem, only the header-freeze/DATA_START_ROW/tail-truncate material is properly in-scope B-side surplus for this specific EARS id; the lock/banner/tab-order material likely belongs to sibling SHEET-TAB-* or SHEET-MARK-* specs not given here and was excluded from the findings above as out-of-scope noise rather than true SHEET-TAB-003 drift. Also worth a passing note (not elevated to a finding, since it can't be verified from the four given files): the real adapter's data range is the open-ended `'{tab}'!A{DATA_START_ROW}:Z` (no end row), and the only place tail-truncation is actually exercised in the given tests is the trivial full-vector-replace in the InMemorySheetsView fake (`existing.rows = tab.rows.clone()`); whether the real low-level SheetsApi/FakeSheetsApi (not among the four files) faithfully reproduces Sheets' real clearing semantics for an open-ended range is unverified here.
